clue.text: An exercise to promote winning

parts.note: to promote something is to push it
a player who is ahead is up

explanation.surface: A workout plan designed to encourage victory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A push-up is a floor exercise lowering and raising the body on the arms.

clue.text: No seats available for replacement husband-to-be

parts.note: a replacement or substitute is a stand-in
a man about to marry is the groom

explanation.surface: A theatre is full, and someone asks for a seat for the stand-in bridegroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing room is the space left for people to stand when every chair is taken.

clue.text: Good man spoke — with hesitation!

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man
spoke means uttered

explanation.surface: A kind man speaks, but haltingly.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer as well as building it: a saint who speaks, but haltingly.
explanation.definitionFit: To stutter is to speak with repeated involuntary pauses.

clue.text: A Frenchman has spoken without decency

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman
spoken, as opposed to written, is oral

explanation.surface: A man from France has said something indecent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoral means lacking any moral sense, without principles or decency.

clue.text: Bombastic duo led off confused

indicators.note: off means out of order or awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pompous pair were led away bewildered.
explanation.definitionFit: Discombobulated is a jokey word for thrown into disarray, bewildered.

clue.text: Gave an account of how trade ran

indicators.note: how asks in what manner the words were set out, signalling their letters arranged anew

explanation.surface: Someone described the way business went.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to tell a story or recount events.

clue.text: I understand there's a jolly flag!

explanation.surface: Someone acknowledges a cheerful banner.
explanation.definitionFit: In radio talk 'Roger' means message received and understood; the Jolly Roger is the pirate skull-and-crossbones banner.

clue.text: Open university about to make an approach

parts.note: open, not hidden, is overt
RE means about or concerning

explanation.surface: The Open University is about to make a move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open university' looks like Britain's distance-learning institution but splits into two pieces. 'to make' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An overture is an opening move or proposal made to someone.

clue.text: Gamble on north being in place

indicators.note: the abbreviation for north is set inside the word for place

parts.note: to place something is to put it
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A bet on the north of the country coming out on top.
explanation.definitionFit: To punt is British slang for placing a bet or taking a gamble.

clue.text: Showed indifference, quiet and sturdy

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet
rugged means strongly built, sturdy

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a matter, staying silent and solid.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting the shoulders briefly is the classic gesture of not caring.

clue.text: Poorly chorister has Sunday off, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: something done poorly is done badly, so the letters are jumbled
with 'has Sunday off' the abbreviation for Sunday is taken away from the singer's word

explanation.surface: A chorister is unwell and gets Sunday off, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has Sunday off' removes S from CHORISTER, leaving CHORITER, which 'Poorly' rearranges. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhetoric is persuasive or showy style in speech, a way of talking.

clue.text: A socially acceptable charge for salt

parts.note: U means upper-class, so socially acceptable, in old British usage
a charge or fee is a rate

explanation.surface: Asking a fair price for table salt.
explanation.walkthrough: U for socially acceptable comes from the 1950s British U and non-U classification of upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry an aurate is a compound formed from gold and an acid, one kind of salt.

clue.text: By the way there's a cap on the uppers

definitions.text: By the way there's a cap on the uppers

parts.words: By the way there's a cap on the uppers
parts.note: on the road (the way) a maximum velocity is set, and uppers, stimulant drugs, are also known as speed, so a cap on them reads as a limit on that drug

explanation.surface: An aside about someone's footwear having a cap fitted over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By the way' looks like a conversational aside but means beside the road; 'uppers' look like parts of shoes but are stimulants, slang 'speed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Road signs post a maximum permitted velocity, a legal cap on how fast drivers may go.

clue.text: Guarantee to follow across river

indicators.note: the word for following stretches across the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: to ensue is to follow on
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A promise to come after someone over the river.
explanation.definitionFit: To make certain of something is to guarantee it.

clue.text: Furore over theatrical flop leaves one with a nasty smell

indicators.note: in a down answer one piece sits over, above, the other

parts.note: a furore is a stink, a public fuss
a show that fails is a bomb

explanation.surface: Uproar over a failed play leaves an unpleasant aftertaste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stink bomb is a prank device that releases a foul odour.

clue.text: Press subject to players — that's incontestable!

indicators.note: subject to means placed under, so in a down answer this piece comes below

parts.note: the players in a show are its cast
to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: Reporters put to the actors something no one can dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Press' looks like journalists but means smoothing clothes. 'that's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cast-iron argument is one so solid it cannot be challenged.

clue.text: Permitted to listen at some volume

indicators.note: for those who listen, the word is heard rather than read, so it sounds like another

parts.note: permitted means allowed

explanation.surface: Being allowed to hear something played fairly loud.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking audibly, so that others can hear, rather than silently.

clue.text: Next door, a radio presenter has a little money in America

parts.note: a disc jockey, DJ, presents a radio show
a cent is a small US coin

explanation.surface: A broadcaster living nearby has a few coins in the US.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjacent means lying beside or neighbouring.

clue.text: Frank is capable and practised

parts.note: able to do something, so one can
practised in the sense of carried out or performed: did

explanation.surface: A man named Frank is skilled and experienced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name but is the adjective; 'and' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank and candid both describe speaking openly and honestly.

clue.text: The high spirits of one in pleasure trip to a Scottish loch?

parts.note: a jaunt is a short trip for pleasure
I is the Roman numeral for one
Loch Ness is the famous lake in the Scottish Highlands

explanation.surface: Someone's cheerful mood on an outing to a Highland lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Jauntiness is a lively, cheerful and buoyant manner.

clue.text: Headgear required seeing trouble start in the city

indicators.note: start means the first letter of the word trouble

parts.note: urban means of or in the city

explanation.surface: A hat needed at the first sign of unrest in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required seeing' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A turban is a long cloth wound around the head.

clue.text: Sofa not quite finished right for me

indicators.note: the sofa word is cut short before its end, losing its final letter

parts.note: a settee is a sofa

explanation.surface: A couch nearly done is just right for the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'me' often refers to the puzzle's compiler. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The compiler of the puzzle is called the setter, so 'me' speaking in the clue is the compiler.

clue.text: Family left, mistaking poor mark

indicators.note: poor shows the remaining letters are a badly made version
family left means the relatives depart, so their word is taken out

parts.note: one's family is one's kin

explanation.surface: A relative leaves after a mistake earns a bad grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Family left' takes KIN out of MISTAKING, leaving MSTAIG, which 'poor' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A stigma is a mark of disgrace attached to someone.

clue.text: Good party — but sober!

parts.note: a rave is a wild party

explanation.surface: A great celebration, yet a solemn one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave and sober both mean serious and solemn.

clue.text: Performers who are a credit to boast about

parts.note: CR is the bookkeeping abbreviation for credit

indicators.note: about here means around or astir, so the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: Entertainers who would make anyone proud to boast of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges BOAST into OBATS. 'who are' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrobats are circus artists who perform gymnastic feats.

clue.text: Torn about accepting a crew's decoration

indicators.note: the scrambled word takes in, or accepts, the other pieces
torn about means the letters of torn are moved about

parts.note: a crew is made up of men

explanation.surface: Ripping off a ship's company's adornment.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's ripping is a red herring: 'Torn' is only the fodder, and 'crew' is taken as the people who man it.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornament is something added to make a thing look attractive.

clue.text: Fitting end to reform having rejected supporter

indicators.note: the end of the word reform gives its final letter
rejected means sent back, so the golfing word is turned round

parts.note: a golf tee supports the ball

explanation.surface: A suitable way to finish reforming after spurning a backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses TEE to EET. 'having' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Meet is an old word for suitable or proper, as in 'meet and right'.

clue.text: The sort of person who turned to weep about direction

parts.note: turned upside down means inverted

indicators.note: the word for weep goes about, around, the compass letter

parts.note: to weep is to sob
N, north, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Someone who started crying about which way to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'who' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: An inverted snob is someone who disdains wealth and prestige and values working-class things, the reverse of a usual snob.
